"Normally, you'd need to send an audience request and wait in the city for your turn, which could take months if not years.
With that being said, the Three Pillars of Heaven have already granted you special permission to visit their estate at your convenience," said one of the guards.
"After all, you're the hero who defeated the Giant Emperor and saved humanity."
Tian Yang had never announced to the world that he defeated Kulas.
However, the news was still spread somehow.
"Is that so?
Then where do I go to meet them?" Yuan then asked.
"I can guide you there," said the guard who handed his own Heavenly Medallion to Yuan.
"Alright."
After signing out of his post, the guard left the city and led Yuan toward the Three Pillars of Heaven.
"If you don't mind me asking, how did you defeat the Giant Emperor?
Was there a trick to it?
I heard that not even six God Realm Cultivators working together were able to hurt him, much less stop him."
"I am much stronger than them.
That's all there is to it," Yuan calmly replied.
"Is that so...
Anyway, I am forever grateful to you for defeating the Giant Emperor.
If you hadn't stopped him, he would've likely pushed all of us to extinction."
The guard continued to lick Yuan's boots for several hours until he realized that Yuan had stopped responding long ago.
Eventually, they arrived at their destination.
"We have arrived at the Three Pillars of Heaven's estate, the Heavenly Manor.
Please wait here for a moment while I announce your presence."
The guard bowed to Yuan before rushing past the group of individuals waiting outside before disappearing inside.
Yuan gave the group a glance before ignoring them to focus on the massive estate in front of him.
'This place reeks of them...' Yuan shook his head inwardly.
Although he may not be able to use his techniques, his senses were left untouched, so he could still sense Eternal Essence, which enveloped the entire place like a blanket.
Several minutes later, the guard returned with someone by his side—a handsome middle-aged man wearing red robes.
When the group beside Yuan saw the man, they immediately bowed.
"We greet Patriarch Sun!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2337 Sun Rouxi’s Position Within the Family
paragraphs: "You must be Tian Yang!"
Patriarch Sun rushed to greet him, completely ignoring the group who greeted him first, not even bothering to give them a glance.
"I was wondering when you would finally visit our Holy Continent! You have no idea how much I have been wanting to speak to you after that day!"
Yuan ignored his enthusiasm and said, "I am here to see Sun Rouxi. How is she?"
"My daughter? She's currently in seclusion. If you want to see her, you'll have to wait until she emerges."
"Wait for her? That could take thousands of years."

"That's unlikely. Since she went into seclusion to finish healing her injuries and not to cultivate, it shouldn't take too long," said Patriarch Sun. "In the meantime, why don't we have a conversation? It's related to my daughter, too."
"Alright."
Yuan nodded and calmly followed him away, leaving the other group speechless.
"Who the hell was that? I have never seen anyone speaking so casually with Patriarch Sun before!"
"Patriarch Sun didn't seem to mind it, either. He must be a big shot. But why don't I recognize him?"
"Patriarch Sun called him Tian Yang, right? I know him."
Everyone there turned to the one who just spoke with anticipation.
"He's the one who showed up near the end of our war with the Giant Race. Apparently, he's the one who defeated the Giant Emperor and ended the war."
"What?! He's the one who defeated the Giant Emperor—the one even six God Realm cultivators working together couldn't defeat?!"
The group erupted in shock upon learning Tian Yang's identity.
Some time later, Patriarch Sun led Yuan into a private room.

After serving some tea, Patriarch Sun spoke in a sincere voice, "Before we begin, I would like to thank you for defeating the Giant Emperor and saving our lives. If it weren't for you... I don't even dare to imagine the consequences of losing the war."
"Un.
Yuan nonchalantly nodded as he sipped on the tea.
Immediately, he could sense his Celestial Qi growing stronger.
"What do you think?" Patriarch Sun smiled after noticing delight in Yuan's eyes, and he proceeded to explain.

"We only recently successfully crafted this tea. Not only does it require extremely rare ingredients, but it also takes a tremendous amount of time and effort to grow. Despite being the Patriarch of the Sun Family, this is only my second time savoring this tea."
"Thank you. It was a delightful experience," Yuan said, gently placing his teacup down.
Patriarch Sun replied, "I would offer you another, but convincing the others to part with even that single cup required considerable effort."
Yuan narrowed his eyes slightly and said, "Let's get straight to the point. What do you want from me?"

Patriarch Sun's expression suddenly turned serious, and he spoke, "Before that, I have a question for you. What is your relationship with my daughter, Sun Rouxi? This is very important for our upcoming topic, so please answer me truthfully."
After a brief moment of silence, Yuan calmly responded, "We're lovers."
He knew there was no point in lying and that there was a very good chance they were already aware of their relationship.
Patriarch Sun barely reacted to Yuan's response, confirming his suspicions.
"How did the two of you meet?" Patriarch Sun continued to ask.
"Does it really matter?"
"No, I am just curious."
"Then you can ask Sun Rouxi herself.
"Unfortunately, she's not very fond of me. She would simply ignore me if I asked."
"Is that why she ran away to the Immortal Monastery?" Yuan inquired.
"That... I guess you can say that."

After a moment of silence, Patriarch Sun continued, "Anyway, let's start the main topic. I don't know how much my daughter has told you about our family, but since you have acknowledged yourself to be Sun Rouxi's lover, you are obligated to join our family."
Yuan then said, "Unfortunately, she didn't tell me anything about her family."
"Then you'll have a lot to learn."

Yuan nodded. He didn't mind joining their family since this was just a trial. He also needed to learn more about the Three Pillars of Heaven since he still lacked Tian Yang's memories after he defeated Kulas and arrived at the Holy Continent.

"Let's start with Sun Rouxi, the eldest child of the Sun Family—a peerless genius whose innate comprehension allows her to create and grasp techniques that none have been able to rival thus far. A good portion of the techniques within our family were created by her, and if she didn't create them, she was involved in their creation one way or another."

"Of course, her talents don't stop there, and she can finish incomplete techniques started by others. Furthermore, she can refine techniques without even mastering them. In terms of talent, Sun Rouxi is definitely at the top, not just within my Sun Family but the entire Three Pillars of Heaven."
"Even though I am the Patriarch of the family, possessing more authority than her, Sun Rouxi's influence throughout the three families far surpasses mine."
Yuan remained silent. Even though he was aware of Sun Rouxi's talents, he didn't expect her position within the Three Pillars of Heaven to be so prestigious.
'To think she made herself sound like some unimportant figure...' Yuan shook his head inwardly.
However, after learning about Sun Rouxi's influence, he became surprised and puzzled about her family's lack of care during her disappearance.

Although Sun Rouxi remained hidden within Tian Yang's world for most of the time, there was no word of her family looking for her. Given their massive influence and unlimited resources, they could've easily found her if they tried even slightly.
Yet, there wasn't even a whisper about it, as if they didn't try to look for her, which was weird considering her talents and value.
Unable to ignore his curiosity, Yuan decided to inquire.
"Why didn't you try looking for her when she ran away from home?" he asked with a slightly narrowed gaze.

chapters.title: Chapter 2338 Heaven's Envoy
paragraphs: "We've spent tens of thousands of years together. Yet her family seemed to have put in zero effort to find her, as if they didn't care if she was missing or dead." Yuan continued in a grim voice.
"Haaa... It's not that we didn't want to look for her," Patriarch Sun responded after releasing a deep sigh.
After a brief moment of silence, he continued, "We wanted to look for her, but we received a prophecy from the Enlightened One."
Yuan raised his eyebrows and asked, "A prophecy that tells you not to search for a missing person? What kind of nonsense is that?"

"It is the Will of Heaven. I have neither the authority nor the reason to question it," Patriarch Sun said with a solemn expression, his eyes clear and unwavering, filled with firm faith in the Enlightened One.
"From what Rouxi told me, the Enlightened One has the ability to commune with 'Heaven' and receive its guidance. Is that correct?"
Patriarch Sun nodded.
"The Enlightened One is Heaven's envoy—a messenger sent by Heaven itself to guide us along the path to glory."
"Then where was the Enlightened One during the war with the Giant Race?" Yuan asked. "He was absent throughout the entire conflict."
"The Enlightened One does not need to act in order to be involved," Patriarch Sun replied calmly. "Even inaction is the Will of Heaven. In the end, we were victorious."
Yuan's eyes narrowed. "No. We won because I stepped in. Without me, this place wouldn't even exist anymore."

Patriarch Sun calmly nodded. "That is true—you were the one who defeated the Giant Emperor. However, the Enlightened One had already foreseen it. We were unaware of this at the time, but after everything ended, he revealed the truth to us. He said that had he intervened, it would have altered our future and caused us to stray from the path of glory."
"What a convenient excuse. And he's a prophet now, too? I thought he could only speak with Heaven."
"You're mistaken. Although the Enlightened One possesses unfathomable power, he is not a prophet, as it was Heaven who foresaw everything. The Enlightened One merely received Heaven's message."
Yuan was beginning to understand why Sun Rouxi disliked her family.
Although he could reveal the truth about the Enlightened One—and the existence behind it—to Patriarch Sun, doing so would be pointless. In fact, he would likely be dismissed as a madman.
"I'd like to meet the Enlightened One. Would that be possible?" Yuan suddenly asked.
Patriarch Sun shook his head and said, "Meeting the Enlightened One is not easy. In fact, even I cannot meet him without his permission."
Yuan lifted an eyebrow.
"Then how does he pass down Heaven's Will?"

"The Enlightened One spends most of his time within the Celestial Chamber. If he wishes to speak with us, he will send out a scroll. Of course, if we wish to speak with him, we leave our messages in the Celestial Hall."
"In that case, do you think I can write a message to him?"
"Of course."
Patriarch Sun retrieved a golden scroll from his spatial ring and placed it on the table before him.

"You may write whatever message you wish to convey here, and I will send it to the Celestial Hall. That said, there is no fixed timeframe for when it will be read. It could be months—perhaps even years before the Enlightened One reads it."
Yuan silently nodded and started writing his message on the scroll with an ink brush.
A short sentence later, Yuan closed the scroll and handed it back to Patriarch Sun.
"Now then, let's talk about your relationship with my daughter," Patriarch Sun said after putting away the scroll.

"Sun Rouxi is the eldest and most talented in our family. Although you have already proven your own capabilities by defeating the Giant Emperor, you'll still need to receive the family's approval before we can officially accept you into our family.
"And how do I acquire said approval?"

"The Sun Family will hold a meeting with all elders one year from now. At the meeting, we will have a simple vote, where they either approve or disapprove of you. To be approved, you'll need to be supported by at least half of the people there. There used to be twenty elders in the family, but after the war, we're down to eight, so you'll need at least approval from four of them."
"In other words, I have a year to make these elders like me, huh?" Yuan mumbled.
"What will happen if I fail to join?" he then asked.
"Then your relationship with my daughter will end."
"I see. Simple enough."

"We will provide you with a living quarter during your one-year stay here. If you ever need anything, you may ask any of the servants around. Until the meeting, you're still my daughter's partner, and we will treat you like one," said Patriarch Sun.
"Any questions for me before I send you to your quarter?"
"What am I not allowed to do during my stay?"

"There are only two rules you must keep in mind. One. Never approach the Celestial Hall, which leads to the Celestial Chamber. Two, do not approach or speak with the Enlightened One unless spoken to first," revealed Patriarch Sun in a solemn voice.
"Failure to do so will result in your execution, even if you're a God Realm cultivator."
"Are you certain you can kill the one who defeated the Giant Emperor?" Yuan asked, a provocative smile on his lips.

Patriarch Sun narrowed his eyes before replying calmly, "You may have defeated the Giant Emperor, but you are still human. Moreover, as long as you remain on the Holy Continent, we hold the advantage. Had our battle with the Giant Emperor taken place here, we likely would have defeated him as well."
Yuan stayed silent, but the smile on his face remained.
"Are you doubting me?" Patriarch Sun couldn't help but ask.
"Of course not. After all, I am already aware of the countless powerful formations that envelope this place," he calmly replied.

chapters.title: Chapter 2339 Like a Cult
paragraphs: "That's all I have for you now. If you don't have any other questions, you may leave. I have already assigned a servant to you, and she's waiting outside," said Patriarch Sun.
Yuan silently nodded and left the room shortly after.
Once outside, his servant greeted him with a polite bow, "I will be in charge of you, Master Tian."
Yuan raised an eyebrow after seeing the servant.
"Jing Ruye?" he muttered with a surprised expression.
The person before him was none other than Jing Ruye.
"What are you doing?" he subconsciously asked.
"I was asked to take care of you by Patriarch Sun," she calmly replied. "Aren't you Rouxi's servant, though?"
Although Sun Rouxi never treated Jing Ruye as a servant and only made her one in name to protect her, Jing Ruye's official status within the family was only slightly above ordinary servants.
"Yes, but Master Sun is currently in seclusion, and I am already familiar with you, so I was chosen for this job," she explained.

Jing Ruye's unfamiliar demeanor made Yuan uneasy. When she lived with him with Sun Rouxi, she'd been carefree and friendly, like an outgoing neighbor. However, she was the opposite at this moment, acting serious and distant, as if they were complete strangers.
"May I guide you to your living quarters now?" Jing Ruye asked, still in a bowing position.
"You don't have to act so formal with me, you know?" Yuan said.
"Sorry, but that is not possible," she replied instantly, almost as if she had already anticipated he'd say such a thing to her.
"Alright.
Yuan understood her position, and not wanting to trouble her, immediately dropped the matter.
"Bring me to my room," he then said.
"Yes, Master Tian."
Jing Ruye finally straightened her body and began leading Yuan to his living quarters, located only a few minutes away from the main household.
"We've arrived."
"Let's have a chat inside, or are you not allowed to follow me inside?" Yuan asked.
"There is no problem with your request," she said. Once they entered the building and closed the door, Jing Ruye immediately released a deep sigh.
"What a pain in the ass," she muttered out loud, returning to her usual demeanor.
"It's good to see you again," Yuan said to her with a smile, acting like their initial meeting never happened.

Jing Ruye rubbed her eyes and sighed again, "It's only been about five hundred years since we last spoke, but it feels like an eternity. After spending so much time outside of this place, I completely forgot how suffocating this place can be."
Jing Ruye walked to a nearby couch and immediately collapsed onto it.
"You have no idea how much I have suffered since returning to this place," she continued in a trembling voice.
Yuan took a seat beside her and asked, "Tell me about it."

"Since Sister Rouxi is the eldest and nearly untouchable in the family, she wasn't punished for her actions. I, on the other hand, was punished for allowing her to run away, even saying things like I helped her escape. Does that even make sense? Who am I to tell her to return? It's not like I can force her."
"How were you punished?" Yuan looked at her with a pitiful gaze.

"They didn't really do much to me at first because I had Sister Rouxi's protection. However, once she entered seclusion, they started treating me like a lowly servant. Even though I am a servant, I am Sister Rouxi's servant, so I barely did any chores, only ones related to her. But now that I am alone, they make me do everything, from washing clothes to cleaning the bathroom, chores usually done by the lowest ranked servants!
"That's it?" Yuan raised an eyebrow. "I was anticipating something much worse."

"Do you have any idea how humiliating that is?!" Jing Ruye snapped at him. "I am an Immortal! I may be a servant, but I am still an Immortal cultivator! How can they make an Immortal do such mundane chores?!"
Yuan shook his head with a smile and said, "Alright, I get it. Now, tell me about Rouxi."

"There's really not much to say. After returning to the family, she focused on recovering, which didn't take long. Then, she was questioned about her relationship with you. Of course, I was also questioned. She wanted to leave again, but she'd have to leave without me this time since I am under constant surveillance. She eventually gave up and entered seclusion."
"Is that so..."
"Now, it's your turn to explain." Jing Ruye then said, glaring at him.
"I came here to see Rouxi, but I also wanted to investigate her family, specifically the one they call 'Enlightened One'," he said.
Jing Ruye's eyes widened at his words, and she hastily responded, "The Enlightened One?! Are you insane?! That'll get you killed!"

Before Yuan could speak, she continued, "The Enlightened One holds unparalleled influence and authority within the Three Pillars of Heaven. If he wishes to kill someone, they will fulfill it without question or hesitation. In a way, this place is like a cult, and they all serve the Enlightened One like he is a real god." "Have you seen him before?" Yuan asked.
"I have. Once. However, no matter how hard I try, I cannot recall his facial features."
After a moment of silence, she asked, "Why are you investigating the Enlightened One?"
"I just have a few questions for him, that's all." Yuan shrugged.

"I don't know why you're so interested in him, but I advise you to stay away from him. Almost everyone who has spoken to him became a different person afterward, almost like they're possessed by something," she sighed.
"Who are these people?"

"Mostly clan heads, sect leaders, and people in prestigious positions. They were all convinced to join the alliance and serve the Three Pillars of Heaven by the Enlightened One." Hearing this, Yuan wondered if the Enlightened One had some sort of mind-controlling technique, which would definitely be troublesome to deal with.

When she lived with him with Sun Rouxi, she'd been carefree and friendly, like an outgoing neighbor.
However, she was the opposite at this moment, acting serious and distant, as if they were complete strangers.
"May I guide you to your living quarters now?" Jing Ruye asked, still in a bowing position.
"You don't have to act so formal with me, you know?" Yuan said.
"Sorry, but that is not possible," she replied instantly, almost as if she had already anticipated he'd say such a thing to her.
"Alright.
Yuan understood her position, and not wanting to trouble her, immediately dropped the matter.
"Bring me to my room," he then said.
"Yes, Master Tian."
Jing Ruye finally straightened her body and began leading Yuan to his living quarters, located only a few minutes away from the main household.
"We've arrived."
"Let's have a chat inside, or are you not allowed to follow me inside?" Yuan asked.
"There is no problem with your request," she said.
Once they entered the building and closed the door, Jing Ruye immediately released a deep sigh.
"What a pain in the ass," she muttered out loud, returning to her usual demeanor.
"It's good to see you again," Yuan said to her with a smile, acting like their initial meeting never happened.
Jing Ruye rubbed her eyes and sighed again, "It's only been about five hundred years since we last spoke, but it feels like an eternity.
After spending so much time outside of this place, I completely forgot how suffocating this place can be."
Jing Ruye walked to a nearby couch and immediately collapsed onto it.
"You have no idea how much I have suffered since returning to this place," she continued in a trembling voice.
Yuan took a seat beside her and asked, "Tell me about it."
"Since Sister Rouxi is the eldest and nearly untouchable in the family, she wasn't punished for her actions.
I, on the other hand, was punished for allowing her to run away, even saying things like I helped her escape.
Does that even make sense?
Who am I to tell her to return?
It's not like I can force her."
"How were you punished?" Yuan looked at her with a pitiful gaze.
"They didn't really do much to me at first because I had Sister Rouxi's protection.
However, once she entered seclusion, they started treating me like a lowly servant.
Even though I am a servant, I am Sister Rouxi's servant, so I barely did any chores, only ones related to her.
But now that I am alone, they make me do everything, from washing clothes to cleaning the bathroom, chores usually done by the lowest ranked servants!
"That's it?" Yuan raised an eyebrow.
"I was anticipating something much worse."
"Do you have any idea how humiliating that is?!" Jing Ruye snapped at him.
"I am an Immortal!
I may be a servant, but I am still an Immortal cultivator!
How can they make an Immortal do such mundane chores?!"
Yuan shook his head with a smile and said, "Alright, I get it.
Now, tell me about Rouxi."
"There's really not much to say.
After returning to the family, she focused on recovering, which didn't take long.
Then, she was questioned about her relationship with you.
Of course, I was also questioned.
She wanted to leave again, but she'd have to leave without me this time since I am under constant surveillance.
She eventually gave up and entered seclusion."
"Is that so..."
"Now, it's your turn to explain." Jing Ruye then said, glaring at him.
"I came here to see Rouxi, but I also wanted to investigate her family, specifically the one they call 'Enlightened One'," he said.
Jing Ruye's eyes widened at his words, and she hastily responded, "The Enlightened One?!
Are you insane?!
That'll get you killed!"
Before Yuan could speak, she continued, "The Enlightened One holds unparalleled influence and authority within the Three Pillars of Heaven.
If he wishes to kill someone, they will fulfill it without question or hesitation.
In a way, this place is like a cult, and they all serve the Enlightened One like he is a real god." "Have you seen him before?" Yuan asked.
"I have.
Once.
However, no matter how hard I try, I cannot recall his facial features."
After a moment of silence, she asked, "Why are you investigating the Enlightened One?"
"I just have a few questions for him, that's all." Yuan shrugged.
"I don't know why you're so interested in him, but I advise you to stay away from him.
Almost everyone who has spoken to him became a different person afterward, almost like they're possessed by something," she sighed.
"Who are these people?"
"Mostly clan heads, sect leaders, and people in prestigious positions.

They were all convinced to join the alliance and serve the Three Pillars of Heaven by the Enlightened One." Hearing this, Yuan wondered if the Enlightened One had some sort of mind-controlling technique, which would definitely be troublesome to deal with.

chapters.title: Chapter 2340 Meeting the Enlightened One
paragraphs: While Yuan spoke with Jing Ruye at his guest house, Patriarch Sun made his way to the Celestial Hall. Before entering, he opened the scroll with Yuan's message in it and read it.
"Ask your 'Heaven' if it knows Zaaran...?" Patriarch Sun tilted his head with a puzzled look on his face after reading Yuan's message, unable to comprehend it.
'Is he looking for someone?' he wondered inwardly.
After making sure the message didn't contain anything malicious, Patriarch Sun entered the Celestial Hall, a massive building located on a floating island in the skies above the Holy Continent.
Upon arriving, Patriarch Sun walked down the hall until he reached the end and stood before a double door exuding divine aura and an otherworldly presence.
Without saying a word, he kowtowed on the ground and bowed to it—to the person inside.
Then, he stood up and placed Yuan's message on the mountain of messages that were already piled up not far away.
Before leaving, Patriarch Sun bowed toward the double doors again.

As he turned and took two steps, the doors behind him slowly opened. Patriarch Sun froze, turning toward the doorway as a bright, divine light poured through, almost as if there was a sun inside the room. A moment later, a silhouette stepped out from the radiant glow.
"Enlightened One." Patriarch Sun greeted him with a deep bow of reverence.
However, the Enlightened One completely ignored him and made a gesture at the mountain of messages, moving them inside his room.
A moment later, he spoke in an authoritative voice, "How are the preparations?"
Patriarch Sun immediately responded, "The preparations are going smoothly with half of the families out there supporting your goal now."
"In that case, proceed to the next step. I want the entire world to bow before me by the end of the year! This is Heaven's Will!" "As you wish..."
Without another word, the Enlightened One disappeared into the light again, and Patriarch Sun left shortly after.
Inside the Celestial Chamber, the Enlightened One began reading the messages at random. Most of them prayed to him, while some prayed for blessings from Heaven.
Eventually, he reached a certain message.
"Ask your 'Heaven' if it knows Zaaran?" The Enlightened One immediately frowned upon recognizing the name Zaaran.
"Which bastard sent me this message?!" he exclaimed.
After a long moment of silence, the Enlightened One activated a certain communication technique.
"Bahrah! We have an issue here! Someone is aware of your existence!" The Enlightened One revealed to the unfathomably massive silhouette before him as the starry sky surrounded them.
"I don't see how that is an issue," said Bahrah.
"What if they try to interfere with our plans like Zaaran did?" The Enlightened One replied.
"Hahaha!" Bahrah laughed out loud. "Zaaran? He's too stupid to ruin my plans. In fact, I was the one to provoke him first, and he fell for it like the idiot he is."
"I-Is that so...?" The Enlightened One wore a dumbfounded look on his face.
"This individual must be the one who stopped Zaaran's invasion. If anything we should be thanking him for saving me some energy."
"What should I do about him?" The Enlightened One asked.
"Nothing... No, I want you to try and recruit him. If I had someone like him under me, our plans will undoubtedly proceed much smoother."
"Y-You want to recruit him?!" The Enlightened One exclaimed in shock.
He opened his mouth only to quickly close it without uttering another word.
'Fuck! What about me? If I recruit that bastard and Bahrah favors him more than me, I could be replaced! I don't want to risk that!'

The Enlightened One was worried that his position might be replaced, but he didn't dare to voice his concerns out loud. "I... I will try," he said after a moment of silence, lacking the courage to reject Bahrah.
A few days later, Jing Ruye asked Yuan, "How long do you intend on staying here?"
"You won't get any approval from the elders by sitting around all day, you know."
"I don't really care about their approval," Yuan calmly replied.
"What...? Then what will you do if you cannot join the family and are forced to end your relationship with Sister Rouxi?"
"Even if they are her family, they have no authority to dictate whether I can be with her or not."
"Do you intend on fighting the Sun Family?" Jing Ruye was speechless.
"If I have to."
Jing Ruye went silent, dumbfounded. Just as she opened her mouth, a knock sounded at the door and interrupted her thoughts.
When she opened the door and saw who was standing outside, she hastily spoke, "T-This servant greets the Patriarch!"
"Is Tian Yang here?" Patriarch Sun asked.
"I am." Yuan responded as he approached the door. "Need something from me?"
"The Enlightened One has summoned you," he said with a solemn look on his face.
"That was quick," Yuan replied with a calm smile.
"He said this was urgent and that you needed to meet him right away."
"Take me to him." Patriarch Sun nodded and led him to the floating island above the Holy Continent.
"Who is Zaaran?" Patriarch Sun suddenly inquired.
"So you read my message, too."
"I had to ensure the contents weren't malicious or offensive," he calmly explained.
Yuan pondered for a moment before responding, "I can tell you about Zaaran, but there is a price to pay."
"What do you want for that information?" Patriarch Sun asked, misunderstanding Yuan's words as wanting payment for such information.
Yuan chuckled and said, "It's nothing like that."
"Whatever the price is, I don't care. Just tell me." Patriarch Sun insisted.
Yuan nodded and said, "Zaaran is an Eternal—a God who lives beyond this world."

Yuan wasn't worried that Patriarch Sun might die since he was a God Realm cultivator and had plenty of longevity to sacrifice. He also wanted to confirm if Patriarch Sun needed to sacrifice his longevity to learn this information as he did.

chapters.title: Chapter 2341 Meeting the Enlightened One(2)
paragraphs: "An Eternal...? A God who lives beyond our world?" Patriarch Sun repeated Yuan's words with a dumbfounded look on his face.
"That's—" Just as Patriarch Sun opened his mouth to speak again, he abruptly froze, a look of excruciating pain twisting across his face.
"Agh!" Patriarch Sun collapsed to the ground, groaning as veins bulged across his face while he struggled to endure the pain.
Seeing this, Yuan reaffirmed that learning about the Eternals required sacrifice. However, this only made him more confused.
'Why didn't Sun Rouxi and Ren Xia experience this?' he wondered inwardly.
The pain disappeared a few moments later, and Patriarch Sun glared at Yuan with killing intent afterward.
"What the hell was that?! What did you do to me?!" he exclaimed as he jumped to his feet and grabbed Yuan by his collar.
"That was the feeling of your longevity being forcefully sacrificed—the price for forbidden knowledge," Yuan calmly replied. "Most people die just learning about their existence."
"Are you insane?! Why would you reveal such information to me then?! What if I had died?!" Patriarch Sun roared.

Yuan smiled and said, "I told you because you asked. But don't worry, there was pretty much zero chance that you'd die from it. After all, as a God Ascension cultivator, you have plenty of longevity."
"God Ascension...? What is that?" Patriarch Sun frowned.
"Oh, right. You guys still call it the God Realm." Yuan muttered after realizing his mistake.

He proceeded to explain, "You may know it as the God Realm, but you're nowhere near becoming a real 'God'. There are nine levels you must ascend before you reach true godhood, hence why we call it God Ascension Realm instead of God Realm."
Patriarch Sun stared at Yuan with a look of disbelief.
"Just...Just who the hell are you, and where did you acquire such profound knowledge?" he asked in a trembling voice as his understanding of Tian Yang quickly shattered.
"I'm from the future," Yuan casually joked.
"What the hell are you—"
Yuan suddenly interrupted, "Let's get moving. The Enlightened One is waiting for us, right? We shouldn't make him wait too long."
Patriarch Sun could only silently nod his head and continued guiding Yuan to the Celestial Hall.
A few minutes later, they arrived at the massive manor known as the Celestial Hall.

'This place... It's the Celestial Palace.' Even though it was smaller and a little different, Yuan immediately recognized the place since he had gone on a slaughtering spree not too long ago in the very same place.
When they stepped inside, Yuan confirmed that the place was the Celestial Palace because it had the same design.
Soon, they arrived at the majestic double door at the end of the hall.
However, Patriarch Sun didn't knock on the door and merely stood there in silence. This continued for a whole minute before Yuan asked out loud, "Aren't you going to tell him that we have arrived?"
Patriarch Sun turned to look him in the eyes and responded with a serious face, "We cannot disturb the Enlightened One, as he could be receiving a divination at any moment."
"Are you telling me that we will have to wait here for him to come out at god-knows-when?"
Patriarch Sun calmly nodded.
'This crazy bastard...' Yuan sighed inwardly.
Suddenly, Patriarch Sun reached into his pocket and retrieved a communication jade slip.
After listening to the message that he'd just received, he said to Yuan, "I have to leave for now. Do not, under any circumstances, disturb the Enlightened One while I am away."
"Okay." Yuan obediently nodded.
After Patriarch Sun left, Yuan waited for another two whole minutes before he approached the door and, without hesitation, knocked on it.
After a few moments of stillness, the double doors abruptly opened just enough for a person to walk out, and a clear and displeased voice resounded.

"Didn't Patriarch Sun just tell you not to disturb me? What an impatient and rude bastard." A moment later, a silhouette emerged from the divine radiance pouring through the open space, and Yuan's eyes narrowed as he focused on its face that was completely blocked by a veil and hood.
"I can have you executed for disturbing me, you know?" said the Enlightened One.
Yuan shrugged and asked, "How long did you intend on making me wait?"
"A few decades." The Enlightened One responded without hesitation.
Yuan chuckled, "Then I made the right choice. Are you really going to execute me for it?"
The Enlightened One remained silent for a moment before responding, "No... at least not right now."
He turned around and disappeared inside the Celestial Chamber.
"Follow me. We have a lot to talk about."
Yuan followed him into the room.
Upon entering the Celestial Chamber, Yuan found himself surrounded by flickering stars in a pitch-black background.
"Do you know what kind of place this is?" The Enlightened One suddenly questioned as he gazed at the void.
"The starry sky, the world beyond our sky."
The Enlightened One turned to face Yuan and said, "True, it's a world beyond ours, but I call it the Celestial Domain, as it is owned and ruled by the Gods."

He continued, "Not only does the Celestial Domain belong to them, so does this world that we live in. We are nothing more than insects in their eyes." "What are you trying to get at?" Yuan asked with a raised eyebrow.
"That it's only normal for us to obey and serve them. So, I have a proposal for you. Join me and serve my God—Bahrah!"
Yuan sighed out loud, "I was wondering what nonsense you were going to say, and it's more pathetic than I anticipated."
"Nonsense? Pathetic?" The Enlightened One frowned.
"Aren't you serving a God as well? Otherwise, how else would you have defeated the Giant Emperor, who was supported by Zaaran?" he asked.
Yuan pondered for a moment before responding, "While I have a connection with an Eternal, I wouldn't say that I am serving him."
The Enlightened One fell silent at his words.

chapters.title: Chapter 2342 Speaking With Bahrah
paragraphs: After a moment of silence, the Enlightened One spoke in a trembling voice, "If you're not serving the Eternal, then are you claiming to be on equal terms with them?"
However, before Yuan could respond, the Enlightened One exploded with anger and roared loudly, "Blasphemy! The Gods are above us! The only equals they have are each other!"
Yuan shrugged.
"I wouldn't say we're equals, but I am definitely not working for them, either."
He had an urge to say that Eternals were beneath him to see how the Enlightened One would react, but he decided not to stir up unnecessary trouble.
The Enlightened One glared at him for a good moment before speaking again, "The God you've been in contact with... What is their name?"
"Sorry, but he told me not to reveal it to anyone, especially if they're already working for another Eternal."
Of course, it was a lie, as Shura never said such a thing.
However, the Enlightened One didn't question it and then said, "Even if you're in contact with another God, it doesn't change my God's orders to recruit you."
"Oh?" Yuan raised an eyebrow at this unexpected situation.
"Your Eternal wants to recruit me? I'm listening."
He didn't immediately refuse since this would help him learn more about the Eternal behind the Enlightened One.
The Enlightened One sucked his teeth after seeing Yuan's unexpected enthusiasm.
"I thought you didn't want to serve the Gods?" "Huh? When did I say that? I merely responded to your question—that I wasn't serving one. I never said that I'd never serve one."
"Hmph! I do not believe you."
"So, when do I get to speak with your God?" Yuan then asked.

"Who the hell do you think you are? Do you think you can speak to my God whenever you want? Unfortunately for you, my God will speak with you when they're ready, and you won't be able to force your way as you did with me."
"Relax. I am just asking a question. Are you always this aggressive? Or do you just dislike me for whatever reason?" Yuan looked at him with a questioning gaze.

"Your entire existence annoys me!" The Enlightened One admitted. "I don't know why, but when I look at you, my entire being feels disgusted! Even now, I am resisting the urge to puke!" "But this is our first time meeting. Or was my first impression really that bad?" Yuan wondered out loud.
"Anyway, if your God isn't going to speak with me right now, I have no reason to linger, so I'll be taking my leave."
"Wait!" The Enlightened One suddenly stopped him. "Who said you could leave?" "Do you want me to stay? I thought my existence disgusted you. If I were you, I'd want me to leave as soon as possible."
"As much as I want you to get out of my sight, I still have some questions for you," he said.
"I can't say I'll be able to answer all of your questions, but feel free to ask them."
"What is your relationship with the Giant Emperor and the God behind him?"

"A tough question right from the get-go, huh?" Yuan smiled. "He was a friend of mine. We've known each other long before he met the Eternal. As for the Eternal... I don't have any relationship with him."
"Then why did you kill the Giant Emperor?"
"Are you asking me why I saved the world from his invasion? Would you have done it if I didn't intervene?" Yuan asked.
The Enlightened One remained quiet for a moment before responding in a clear voice, "Of course, I would've stopped him. In fact, if you had waited a day later, I would've already taken care of him."
"And how would you have done that?" Yuan pressed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2343 Bahrah's Challenge
paragraphs: "That Saaruk! He's much slyer than I expected! He makes himself look like an idiot, but he's actually scheming behind our backs!" Bahrah muttered.

He then focused on Yuan and spoke, "Instead of working for Saaruk, why don't you work for me instead? I don't know what Saaruk promised you, but I can promise you this world and unlimited authority. I will make you its supreme ruler, second to none and above every living being to walk this earth."

"That is a tempting offer, considering that Saaruk didn't really promise me anything except some of his powers." Bahrah laughed at such words and continued, "In that case, you should definitely ditch that idiot and come work for me! In fact, it's only a matter of time before we conquer this world—not with force like Zaaran but strategy and faith."
"Is that why you've been forming an alliance with everyone?"
Yuan already knew their plans but still asked anyway.
"Indeed. This plan started long before Zaaran's interference. Although it was a risky move, I made his puppet kill someone from the Three Pillars of Heaven, forcing Zaaran's hands."
Yuan's eyebrows twitched slightly after hearing this revelation.
'Is that why Kulas went on a rampage even though I was near him at that time? So it was this bastard's doing...'
"What would you have done if I never intervened?" Yuan suddenly asked.
"I have my own ways," said Bahrah with a mysterious smirk on its face.
"What about the Enlightened One, then? If I am going to be second to none, that must include him, you know?"
"Hahaha! There's no problem at all! He might be a little angry, but there's nothing he can do about it!"
"So you're just going to discard him like this?" Yuan sneered. "How am I supposed to work with someone who doesn't hesitate to throw away their own pawn?"

"I am not going to discard him. He's still useful, and there are other things he can do for me. If you're worried that I might do the same to you, then you don't have to worry, since you are countless times better than that kid. However, you still have to prove yourself."
Yuan pondered for a moment before nodding, "Alright, I'll work with you for now. What do you want me to do?"
"I want you to surpass the Enlightened One's authority within the Three Pillars of Heaven."
"Surpass him? That is not going to be simple..." Yuan muttered.
Bahrah laughed. "I never said it would be easy. Did you really think I'd just hand everything to you? If you want his position, you'll have to take it yourself.

He continued calmly, "That said, without a handicap, it would be impossible for you. He's amassed immense influence and faith over the years, while you're nothing more than a stranger who appeared out of nowhere."
"Ten thousand years. I will make it so that the Enlightened One cannot interfere with you for ten thousand years, so try your best to defeat him in that time."
"So he'll also be aware of our little competition?" Yuan asked.
"Of course."
"Very well. I accept the challenge."
"See you again in ten thousand years... if you're still alive by then!"
In the next moment, Yuan found himself back in the Celestial Chamber with the Enlightened One.
"What did you speak to my God about?" The Enlightened One immediately questioned.
"You should ask him yourself."
"What are you—"
The Enlightened One suddenly halted his speech and stood there in silence, almost as if he was in a daze.
'So that's how it looks when I am speaking with an Eternal...' Yuan thought to himself, as this was his first time seeing someone in a conversation with one.
Moments later, the Enlightened One started to move again.
"So you dare covet my position..." he growled, his voice low and feral, like a threatened beast.
"It wasn't my idea, but your God's, you know?" "I don't care! I will never hand my position over to someone like you!" the Enlightened One roared as he suddenly lunged at Yuan.
Yuan stepped aside casually, causing the Enlightened One to stumble and crash to the ground.
Yuan narrowed his eyes at him. During the fall, the Enlightened One's veil and hood had slipped away, revealing his face.
'Celestial Emperor...'
Yuan instantly recognized his handsome face. The Enlightened One turned out to be the first Celestial Emperor.
However, Yuan wasn't surprised in the slightest, as if he already suspected this when he couldn't sense any cultivation from the Enlightened One.
"I was wondering why I couldn't sense your cultivation. To think you're just a mere mortal..." Yuan spoke with a cold smile.
The Enlightened One's expression paled.
"W-What nonsense are you spouting?! I'm merely concealing my cultivation!" he shouted, panic seeping into his voice as he desperately tried to hide the truth.
Unfortunately for him, his lies held no weight with Yuan, who already knew the truth.
Yuan suddenly reached for his neck and dragged him off the ground and into the air.

"I was given ten thousand years to replace you. At first, I thought it would be pretty difficult. But now... I don't even need a day, as I can simply replace you by killing you," he spoke in a cold voice.
"Y-You wouldn't dare! If you kill me, the Three Pillars of Heaven and half of the world will turn into your enemy! At that point, you will no longer be able to rule the world!"
Yuan fell silent for a moment before releasing him.
"Don't worry. It would be far too easy—and boring—to simply kill you," he said in a grim voice. "I want you to watch as I slowly usurp your authority and replace you."
The Enlightened One glared at Yuan with teary eyes as he lay on the ground, yet there was nothing he could do, as Bahrah had forbidden him from interfering with Yuan for the next ten thousand years.

chapters.title: Chapter 2344 Becoming Heaven's Envoy
paragraphs: "Y-You... I forbid it!" The Enlightened One bit his lips to resist his fear and shouted at Yuan.
"This position belongs to me! I worked nonstop for over 100,000 years to reach my current status! Who the hell are you to just appear and try take it away from me?! You don't deserve it!"

Yuan chuckled and replied, "You think you deserve this position? If it weren't for the Eternal, you wouldn't even be alive right now, you idiot. And all you do is order people around and relay the Eternal's message, pretending to be heaven's envoy. If you think about it, you've really done nothing deserving of your position, hence why your Master wants me, someone more competent and useful, to replace you."

The Enlightened One's face drained of color. Even though Yuan had yet to begin usurping his position, the mere weight of his presence was enough to make him feel threatened. Worse still, Yuan had Bahrah's backing, while he himself was forbidden to act—forced to stand by and watch as Yuan slowly replaced him.
"Be a good little boy and stay here. I have a lot to do." Yuan turned around and began making his way toward the exit.
Seeing this, the Enlightened One rushed to block the door with his own body, arms spread and everything.
"How cute." Yuan chuckled before walking around him. "There's nothing you can do to stop me, so just sit back and enjoy whatever time you have left in that position."
The Enlightened One trembled.
"No! I haven't even achieved my dream of being the supreme ruler of this world yet! There's no way I will let you take it from me!"
The Enlightened One then spoke with a determined look on his face, "I may not be able to directly interfere with you, but it's not like there's nothing I can do!"
Meanwhile, Patriarch Sun returned to the Celestial Hall after dealing with his business.
"What the...? He's gone?"
He was dumbfounded to find Yuan missing from the Celestial Hall.
"Did he leave... or did he enter the Celestial Chamber to meet with the Enlightened One?"
Patriarch Sun pondered for a moment before abandoning his latter thought, as there was no way the Enlightened One would invite someone to his chamber.
"After all, even I have not been inside the Celestial Chamber..." Patriarch Sun shook his head.
Just as he was about to turn around and leave in search of Yuan, the double doors swung open, and two figures emerged from the light.

Patriarch Sun's eyes widened in disbelief as Yuan's face came into clear view. Yet his shock did not end there. The Enlightened One stood right behind him, his veil and hood gone, his face fully exposed.
"Your Majesty!"
Despite his shock, Patriarch Sun subconsciously greeted the Enlightened One.
Yuan raised an eyebrow at the way Patriarch Sun addressed the Enlightened One as if he were already the Celestial Emperor.
"Your Majesty?" Yuan looked at the Enlightened One and poked fun at him. "Even though you have not unified the world yet?"
"S-Shut up!" Patriarch Sun lifted his head to stare at them with a bewildered expression.
"T-Tian Yang... Y-You..."
"Hm?" Yuan quickly realized why Patriarch Sun was staring at him in disbelief and smiled. "Don't worry, we've become best friends."
Yuan suddenly wrapped his arm around the Enlightened One's shoulders as if they were best buddies.
"Get your filthy hands off me, you crazy bastard!" The Enlightened One swiftly pushed Yuan's arm away.
"Tian Yang! What have you done?!" Patriarch Sun exclaimed in anger. "Touching His Majesty is forbidden and punishable by death!"
"Oh? Are you going to execute me for touching you, 'Your Majesty'?" Yuan asked the Enlightened One with a cold smile.
'Go ahead and execute me. I'll kill you before that happens.'
Yuan suddenly spoke using voice transmission, causing the Enlightened One to tremble in fear.
"Your Majesty!" Patriarch Sun glared at him.
After a moment of silence, the Enlightened One spoke, "It's fine.
"What?!" Patriarch Sun almost couldn't believe his ears.

"What did I say? We're best friends." Yuan chuckled. "After all, I have also become Heaven's Envoy after speaking with Heaven itself!" "WHAT?!" The Enlightened One and Patriarch Sun exclaimed. 'This sly bastard! I didn't think he'd use me to turn himself into Heaven's Envoy!' The Enlightened One cried inwardly after realizing his mistake.
"Why are you so surprised?" Yuan asked the Enlightened One. "We just finished speaking with 'Heaven'. Or are you saying that I am lying?"
"..." The Enlightened One gritted his teeth.
If he were to invalidate Yuan's claim, he'd be interfering with Yuan and denying Heaven's Will. In other words, defying Bahrah's orders.
"I-It's true..." he spoke in a trembling voice. "He has spoken with Heaven and received its approval..."
"T-This is...!" Patriarch Sun was speechless.
Yuan couldn't help but laugh inwardly.
'Oh, Celestial Emperor... you're too young and naive right now, making it incredibly easy to manipulate you!'

Having spent most of his time in isolation within the Celestial Chamber and rarely interacting with others, the Enlightened One lacked real experience. Moreover, a lifetime of absolute authority had left him surrounded by a fragile wall of perceived safety. Yet that same fragility meant that once someone shattered that illusion and stepped into his personal domain as a threat, he had no idea how to respond and would panic easily.
Furthermore, Yuan had already instilled fear in the Enlightened One with a genuine threat of death, making it even harder for him to think clearly.

Yuan took advantage of this situation and spoke again, "Not only have I received Heaven's approval, but I have also received many divinations from Heaven that will allow me to unify the world within ten thousand years."
"What?! That's impossible!" The Enlightened One exclaimed.

Yuan looked at him with a puzzled face and said, "Didn't Heaven tell you? I guess Heaven is really disappointed by your underwhelming performance, hence why it asked me to take charge." "Y-You...!" The Enlightened One gritted his teeth and trembled in anger, but his mind was in too much of a mess to think of a proper response.

That's impossible!" The Enlightened One exclaimed.
Yuan looked at him with a puzzled face and said, "Didn't Heaven tell you?

I guess Heaven is really disappointed by your underwhelming performance, hence why it asked me to take charge." "Y-You...!" The Enlightened One gritted his teeth and trembled in anger, but his mind was in too much of a mess to think of a proper response.

chapters.title: Chapter 2345 Becoming Heaven's Envoy(2)
paragraphs: Patriarch Sun watched Yuan and the Enlightened One with a gawking expressing, as he'd never seen anyone speaking and treating the Enlightened One like an equal.
In fact, Yuan even appeared superior in Patriarch Sun's eyes. There was just something about him that made the Enlightened One's presence feel weaker than usual.
"Patriarch." Yuan suddenly called out to him.
"Y-Yes?!" Patriarch Sun hastily responded after snapping out of his daze.
"Your Majesty...?" he added after a brief pause.
"Your Majesty?" Yuan frowned. "Do I look like an emperor to you? Just continue calling me like before."
"As you wish, Senior Tian..."
Even though Yuan had just announced his position as Heaven's Envoy, his presence and confidence were so overwhelming that Patriarch Sun subconsciously treated him as if he were the Enlightened One.
"Anyway, I want you to summon everyone in the family, so I can officially announce my presence to the entire family."
"I will have everyone assemble at the Heavenly Assembly as soon as possible!" Patriarch Sun acknowledged.
"You may leave now," said Yuan.
"Yes!"
Patriarch Sun didn't linger to ask any more questions and disappeared in the blink of an eye.
Once they were alone again, the Enlightened One cursed at Yuan, "How dare you use me as a stepping stone, you damn bastard!"
Yuan shrugged.
"If you don't want me to use you as a stepping stone, you're free to surrender your position to me. I can even promise to let you live in peace for the rest of your life."

"You expect me to surrender to a nobody like you? In your dreams!" the Enlightened One roared, a ferocious flame burning in his eyes. "Even if I cannot interfere with you directly, I can still continue to expand my influence! I will make sure you never defeat me, no matter how hard you try and prove my worth to God!"
Yuan abruptly placed a hand on the Enlightened One's head and proceeded to rub it fiercely, messing with his hair like an elder brother bullying a younger sibling.
"Good luck with that," he laughed out loud as he left the Celestial Hall, leaving the Enlightened One trembling in anger.

'Seriously! Where in God's name did such a bastard come from?!' The Enlightened One clenched his fists and gritted his teeth at Yuan's very existence, feeling emotions he never knew existed before—mostly anger.
After leaving, Patriarch Sun summoned every member of the three families to the Heavenly Assembly using the summoning bell—an instrument reserved only for emergencies.
The bell's toll echoed across the Holy Continent, sending shock through everyone who heard it.
"This sound... It's Heaven's Bell! Who the hell rang it?!" "It wasn't used even during our war with the Giant Race, yet it's being used now?! What in heaven's name happened?!"
"Everyone! Stop whatever you are doing and head to the Heavenly Assembly!"

In just a few hours, tens of thousands of people from the Three Pillars of Heaven gathered at the Heavenly Assembly. Whether it was a mere servant or a high-ranking elder, everyone had to be there with no exception.
"Patriarch Sun! Were you responsible for ringing the Heavenly Bell?!"
A beautiful middle-aged woman questioned him.
"Indeed, I rang the Heavenly Bell."
"You'd better have a good explanation for this, Patriarch Sun!" Another voice resounded.
"Calm down, Patriarch Ji. Everything will be explained in a moment. However, I will not be the one speaking."
"Wait a second..." The middle-aged woman who questioned him earlier realized something and asked, "Is this related to His Majesty, the Enlightened One?"
The entire atmosphere changed upon hearing the Enlightened One's name.
Patriarch Sun responded with only a silent nod.
Now that they knew the Enlightened One was involved, nobody there dared ask any more questions.
Some time later, a figure appeared on the platform beside Patriarch Sun.
"Who the hell is that? And why is he standing there?"
Among the thousands of people there, only a few recognized Yuan's face, so the majority were puzzled by his random appearance.
"Hello, everyone. My name is Tian Yang, and I was the one who called for you."
Yuan wasted no time and immediately introduced himself.
However, before he could say another word, someone shouted, "Tian Yang?! Who the fuck is that?! Get out of there! His Majesty, the Enlightened One, will be here soon!
Many more voices followed right after, all of them cursing at Tian Yang.
Seeing this, Patriarch Sun, without a word, unleashed his cultivation base and attacked those who had just spoken, instantly killing them on the spot.

"Patriarch Sun?!" The Family Heads and Elders exclaimed in shock after witnessing his sudden and brutal response, especially since the first victim to speak was actually a high-ranking Elder. "What is the meaning of this?! Why did you kill Elder Wu?!" Patriarch Ji demanded an answer, as Elder Wu was from his Ji Family.
"Those who dare to interrupt and disrespect Heaven's Envoy will be executed on the spot!" Patriarch Sun declared.
"WHAT!??!"
Everyone there exclaimed in shock.
"B-But the Enlightened One isn't even present! And they were talking to—"
They looked at Yuan, who stood calmly before them, faces puzzled.
"Let me finish," Yuan said before continuing, "I have spoken to Heaven and been accepted as its second Heaven's Envoy."
Silence rippled throughout the crowd after his declaration as a second Heaven's Envoy.
Someone suddenly raised his hand.
Yuan pointed at him and asked, "What is it?"

"I am the patriarch of the Tian Family, Tian Liuming. I would like to ask you... How did this happen? And do you have evidence? Even if I want to believe you, it's simply too sudden and hard to believe, especially since this is the first time many of us have even heard of you."
"A good question. Allow me to explain everything from the beginning," said Yuan.
"Initially, I came here to check up on Sun Rouxi, my partner. However, I was also curious about the Enlightened One, so I asked him to meet with me."
"Sun Rouxi?! Your partner?!"
The crowd was already in shock—and Yuan was only just beginning.

chapters.title: Chapter 2346 Convincing the Three Pillars of Heaven
paragraphs: "The Enlightened One, perhaps having sensed something familiar within me, agreed to meet me, even inviting me into his Celestial Chamber to chat." Yuan continued, sprinkling some nonsense into his truth, making it seem as if the Enlightened One already knew that he'd become Heaven's second envoy.

"The moment I entered the Celestial Chamber, I sensed a heavenly aura descend upon me, and that's when I met and had a conversation with Heaven, who wanted me to be its second envoy because the Enlightened One was lacking something that I possessed."

"The Enlightened One is lacking?! That's blasphemy!" Patriarch Ji exclaimed in disbelief. "It's because of His Majesty that we are able to live peacefully! His contributions to this world are endless, and he was also the first one to discover Celestial Qi!"
Yuan calmly replied, "I am not denying the Enlightened One's achievements. Unfortunately, it wasn't enough to satisfy Heaven, hence why I am here right now."
He narrowed his eyes slightly and continued, "Or are you refuting Heaven's Will?"
"T-That wasn't my intention..." Patriarch Ji swallowed nervously.
Matriarch Tian suddenly raised her hand and asked, "Do you have any evidence to prove your claim of being Heaven's second envoy?"
Yuan turned to look at Patriarch Sun and said, "Patriarch Sun is my evidence, as he was there as a witnessness."

Patriarch Sun nodded and revealed, "When I was at the Celestial Hall, I watched him and the Enlightened One emerge from the Celestial Chamber together. Not only that, but the Enlightened One also treated him like an equal, even removing his hood and face veil. If you doubt my words, I am willing to swear an oath."

"But that only proves he went inside the Celestial Chamber with the Enlightened One and became acquainted with each other... It, in no way, proves that he was chosen by Heaven to be its second envoy." Patriarch Tian said with a doubtful look on his face.
Yuan then asked, "In that case, may I ask how the Enlightened One proved himself?"

One of the Elders answered at once, "His Majesty revealed countless cultivation techniques and pill recipes through Heaven's Will—knowledge that had never existed before—propelling the cultivation world forward by leaps and bounds!"
"That's it?" Yuan asked, one eyebrow raised, clearly unimpressed.
"H-He would also occasionally receive prophecies—visions of the future!" the Elder hurriedly added. "Our war with the Giant Race is one of many such examples!"
Although Yuan could argue these claims, he decided not to expose himself as someone trying to challenge the Enlightened One for now.
And instead of refuting them, he said, "If it's just pill recipes and cultivation techniques, I have also received many of them from Heaven, and I am willing to share them to prove myself."
As someone who has lived multiple lifetimes and has hundreds of millions of years of experience, there was nobody in this world who possessed as much knowledge as him—not even close.

"How do we know that these techniques and pill recipes are truly from Heaven? What if you created them yourself?" Another Elder suddenly questioned. "When the Enlightened One shared his techniques, he was not even a hundred years old, so it was impossible for him to have prepared them beforehand. You, on the other hand, had plenty of time."
After a moment of silence, Yuan sighed and said, "You know what? I have a better method to prove myself. Give me a moment. I will be right back.
Before anyone could say another word, Yuan disappeared from the platform like a ghost.
Minutes later, he returned, but he was not alone, and he'd returned with the Enlightened One by his side.
"Y-Your Majesty!"
Everyone there subconsciously lowered their heads the moment they realized it was him, so they were unable to see the anger on his face.
"Enlightened One, my dear friend," Yuan said loudly. "Why don't you serve as my proof and tell everyone here that Heaven has chosen me as its second envoy?"
'You know what will happen if you refuse, right?' Yuan then said to him using voice transmission.
'I will cripple you in front of everyone before killing you like a pig.'
The Enlightened One began to tremble, the threat shattering his resolve as every thought of resisting Yuan vanished in an instant.
"It... It's true... Heaven has chosen him as its second envoy..."
Even though he wasn't forced to lie or anything, the Enlightened One still felt disgusted, as if he'd just stepped on shit. Yet, there was nothing he could do right now but endure it.
'Just you wait, you bastard! I will make sure to repay this humiliation a thousand-fold, no matter how long it takes!' he cursed inwardly.
With the Enlightened One's confirmation, any doubt about Yuan's identity had been washed away, and he was quickly accepted as the second Heaven's Envoy by the Three Pillars of Heaven.
Yuan dismissed everyone at the assembly but the Family Heads shortly after.
"I know this may be too sudden for you, but it's just as sudden for me, so I will need some time to organize myself. I'll contact you again once I am ready," he said to them.
"Take as much time as you need, Your Majesty."
"You can just address me as Senior Tian. I don't like too much formality."
"I understand..."
"About your living quarters... we'll prepare something more fitting for you as soon as possible," said Patriarch Sun.
"There's no need. I am satisfied with my current place."
"As you wish..."
Some time later, Yuan returned to his living quarters. When he arrived, he noticed two people standing at the doorstep.
One of them was Jing Ruye, and the other was Sun Rouxi, who had emerged from her seclusion shortly before Yuan entered the Celestial Chamber.
Yuan wasn't surprised by her appearance since he already noticed her during the assembly.
"It's been a while, Rou—"
"I need to speak with you in private," Sun Rouxi suddenly interrupted, wearing a serious expression on her face.
"Okay."
Without another word, they entered the building while Jing Ruye remained outside.
"What's wrong? Are you upset that I came here?" Yuan asked.
However, Sun Rouxi didn't respond. She merely stood there, silently inspecting him from head to toe.
"Rouxi...?" Yuan raised his eyebrows, looking confused by her actions.
After another moment of silence, Sun Rouxi spoke in a solemn voice, "I will get straight to the point."
She took a deep breath before continuing, "Who... the hell are you?"
"Eh?" Yuan's eyes widened with surprise at her unexpected question.
"What do you mean? It's me, Tian—"
"Stop right there," Sun Rouxi said flatly. "You may look like Tian Yang and sound like him, and you may have convinced others, but you won't fool me."
Yuan was truly bewildered by this situation.
After pondering for a bit, he spoke, "If I am not Tian Yang, then how do I know about..."
He proceeded to recall specific information about her and their time together—something that only the two of them would know.
Sun Rouxi gritted her teeth, glaring at him with blazing fury.
"What the hell did you do to Tian Yang?!" she roared. "Did you steal his memories?!"
Her cultivation erupted as she spoke, surging outward without restraint.

chapters.title: Chapter 2347 Imposter
paragraphs: "Calm down, Rouxi!" Yuan shouted in a somewhat panicked voice as her overwhelming pressure descended on him like a mountain collapsing from above.
"I never gave you permission to use my name, you damn imposter!" Sun Rouxi snapped, her aura growing more violent and powerful.
'Seriously, what the hell is going on?!' Yuan cried inwardly, completely bewildered and puzzled by the situation.
'Is this part of the trial?' he couldn't think of another reason why Sun Rouxi was acting like this.
"I will give you one last chance! Identify yourself! And tell me what you did to Tian Yang!" Sun Rouxi shouted as she retrieved her golden wheel, her entire being seeping with immense killing intent.
After a moment of silence, Yuan replied, "My name is Yuan. I may not be the Tian Yang you know, but I am definitely Tian Yang."
"What bullshit is that?!" she sneered, refusing to believe him.
This left him perplexed, as he couldn't think of any other explanation that wouldn't sound even more crazy.
Eventually, Yuan sighed and asked, "How can you tell that I am not Tian Yang?"
"Your soul," she calmly replied.

"I have never told anyone, but I had developed a technique that allows me to see another's soul, and your soul is completely different from Tian Yang. No... It's actually similar, but it's too old to be Tian Yang."
"My soul, huh?" Yuan muttered.
"Then can you tell how old my soul is?" he then asked.
"I cannot, but I tell that it's old. In fact, it's much older than anything I have seen before. Just how old are you?"
"If we're only talking about the age of my soul, which has experienced several reincarnations and multiple different eras... at least a few hundred million, I guess."
"Several hundred million years old?! There's no way! I doubt this world is even that old!" she exclaimed.
Yuan shrugged, "I don't know what else to tell you."
Sun Rouxi was speechless, but she eventually asked, "What happened to Tian Yang? Is he still alive?"
"Well..."
Yuan wasn't sure how to explain further.
"Actually—"
Right as he opened his mouth, the entire building shook violently.
"What the...? An earthquake?" Sun Rouxi looked around. "No, that shouldn't be possible. The entire continent is protected by formations that prevent these sorts of disturbances!"
Yuan spread his divine sense, but he couldn't see anything out of the ordinary.
A few seconds later, the building... No, the entire world trembled again.
'Is this caused by an Eternal?' Yuan wondered inwardly.
The shaking did not stop. In fact, it grew more frequent and violent.
Yuan turned to look at Sun Rouxi and said, "Let's postpone this conversation for later. Right now, we need to—"
Before he could finish his sentence, Yuan's vision blurred, and he found himself in a familiar place.
"What the...?"
He was suddenly back inside the Stairway to Heaven.
"Tian'er, what is going on?" he asked out loud.
In the next moment, Tian'er emerged from the void with a troubled face.
"I apologize for interrupting your trial, Master, but we have a situation," she said. "Some troublemakers are attacking the Stairway to Heaven," she proceeded to explain.
"What?" Yuan raised an eyebrow.

"Under normal circumstances, this wouldn't be a cause for concern," she said. "But this situation is different. We're being attacked by multiple individuals simultaneously, across several realms. Moreover, these people are wielding a power that is similar to Eternal Essence."
Although it was forbidden to attack the Stairway to Heaven, this wasn't the first time someone had attempted to force their way inside. Of course, none had ever come close to succeeding.
"At this rate, they might actually be able to force their way in," Tian'er said, worry etched across her face as she bit her nails.
"Is there anything I can do?" Yuan asked.
Tian'er shook her head and said, "I'll do something about it. Unfortunately, this means you'll be unable to continue the trial, and you'll have to return later.
"That's fine."
"Then I'll send you to 'that' place right now."
"Alright. Stay safe."
Tian'er snapped her fingers, creating a portal before Yuan.
Yuan had a lot of questions for Tian'er, but with how urgent she seemed, he decided to save them for next time.
"Don't forget about me!" Kulas' voice resounded as his soul appeared beside Yuan.
The next moment, Yuan stepped into the portal, disappearing from the Stairway to Heaven.
Once Kulas also entered the portal, Tian'er immediately activated the Stairway to Heaven's defensive features, something that had never been utilized until this moment.
Meanwhile, outside the Stairway to Heaven, the troublemakers across different realms were taken by surprise when the Stairway to Heaven suddenly vanished into thin air.
"What the? Where did it go?"
"Damn it! I was so close to cracking it open!"
With the Stairway to Heaven gone, the troublemakers did not linger and quickly left the scene.
The Stairway to Heaven's sudden disappearance was quickly noticed, and word spread like wildfire throughout the Nine Heavens, plunging all nine realms into chaos.
"What?! The Stairway to Heaven vanished?! That's impossible!"
"It's true! I saw it with my own eyes—it was gone! And at the location where the Stairway once stood... There were corpses everywhere!"
"If the Stairway to Heaven is gone, how will people traverse between worlds now?"
"It'll likely be impossible for the majority of people, and only those who can traverse the starry sky will be able to move between realms."
"I heard from a friend that he witnessed from afar someone attacking the Stairway to Heaven right before it disappeared!"
"That must be why it disappeared! What kind of lunatic would attack the Stairway to Heaven—and for what reason?! It's like burning the only bridge across a raging river!"
"My only concern right now is whether the Stairway to Heaven will return..."
In just a few days, news of the Stairway to Heaven's disappearance reached almost every single ear in the Nine Heavens.
Of course, this included the Celestial Emperor, who was just as baffled as everyone.

sentences.text: "Calm down, Rouxi!" Yuan shouted in a somewhat panicked voice as her overwhelming pressure descended on him like a mountain collapsing from above.
"I never gave you permission to use my name, you damn imposter!" Sun Rouxi snapped, her aura growing more violent and powerful.
'Seriously, what the hell is going on?!' Yuan cried inwardly, completely bewildered and puzzled by the situation.
'Is this part of the trial?' he couldn't think of another reason why Sun Rouxi was acting like this.
"I will give you one last chance!
Identify yourself!
And tell me what you did to Tian Yang!" Sun Rouxi shouted as she retrieved her golden wheel, her entire being seeping with immense killing intent.
After a moment of silence, Yuan replied, "My name is Yuan.
I may not be the Tian Yang you know, but I am definitely Tian Yang."
"What bullshit is that?!" she sneered, refusing to believe him.
This left him perplexed, as he couldn't think of any other explanation that wouldn't sound even more crazy.
Eventually, Yuan sighed and asked, "How can you tell that I am not Tian Yang?"
"Your soul," she calmly replied.
"I have never told anyone, but I had developed a technique that allows me to see another's soul, and your soul is completely different from Tian Yang.
No...
It's actually similar, but it's too old to be Tian Yang."
"My soul, huh?" Yuan muttered.
"Then can you tell how old my soul is?" he then asked.
"I cannot, but I tell that it's old.
In fact, it's much older than anything I have seen before.
Just how old are you?"
"If we're only talking about the age of my soul, which has experienced several reincarnations and multiple different eras... at least a few hundred million, I guess."
"Several hundred million years old?!
There's no way!
I doubt this world is even that old!" she exclaimed.
Yuan shrugged, "I don't know what else to tell you."
Sun Rouxi was speechless, but she eventually asked, "What happened to Tian Yang?
Is he still alive?"
"Well..."
Yuan wasn't sure how to explain further.
"Actually—"
Right as he opened his mouth, the entire building shook violently.
"What the...?
An earthquake?" Sun Rouxi looked around.
"No, that shouldn't be possible.
The entire continent is protected by formations that prevent these sorts of disturbances!"
Yuan spread his divine sense, but he couldn't see anything out of the ordinary.
A few seconds later, the building...
No, the entire world trembled again.
'Is this caused by an Eternal?' Yuan wondered inwardly.
The shaking did not stop.
In fact, it grew more frequent and violent.
Yuan turned to look at Sun Rouxi and said, "Let's postpone this conversation for later.
Right now, we need to—"
Before he could finish his sentence, Yuan's vision blurred, and he found himself in a familiar place.
"What the...?"
He was suddenly back inside the Stairway to Heaven.
"Tian'er, what is going on?" he asked out loud.
In the next moment, Tian'er emerged from the void with a troubled face.
"I apologize for interrupting your trial, Master, but we have a situation," she said.
"Some troublemakers are attacking the Stairway to Heaven," she proceeded to explain.
"What?" Yuan raised an eyebrow.
"Under normal circumstances, this wouldn't be a cause for concern," she said.
"But this situation is different.
We're being attacked by multiple individuals simultaneously, across several realms.
Moreover, these people are wielding a power that is similar to Eternal Essence."
Although it was forbidden to attack the Stairway to Heaven, this wasn't the first time someone had attempted to force their way inside.
Of course, none had ever come close to succeeding.
"At this rate, they might actually be able to force their way in," Tian'er said, worry etched across her face as she bit her nails.
"Is there anything I can do?" Yuan asked.
Tian'er shook her head and said, "I'll do something about it.
Unfortunately, this means you'll be unable to continue the trial, and you'll have to return later.
"That's fine."
"Then I'll send you to 'that' place right now."
"Alright.
Stay safe."
Tian'er snapped her fingers, creating a portal before Yuan.
Yuan had a lot of questions for Tian'er, but with how urgent she seemed, he decided to save them for next time.
"Don't forget about me!" Kulas' voice resounded as his soul appeared beside Yuan.
The next moment, Yuan stepped into the portal, disappearing from the Stairway to Heaven.
Once Kulas also entered the portal, Tian'er immediately activated the Stairway to Heaven's defensive features, something that had never been utilized until this moment.
Meanwhile, outside the Stairway to Heaven, the troublemakers across different realms were taken by surprise when the Stairway to Heaven suddenly vanished into thin air.
"What the?
Where did it go?"
"Damn it!
I was so close to cracking it open!"
With the Stairway to Heaven gone, the troublemakers did not linger and quickly left the scene.
The Stairway to Heaven's sudden disappearance was quickly noticed, and word spread like wildfire throughout the Nine Heavens, plunging all nine realms into chaos.
"What?!
The Stairway to Heaven vanished?!
That's impossible!"
"It's true!
I saw it with my own eyes—it was gone!
And at the location where the Stairway once stood...
There were corpses everywhere!"

"It'll likely be impossible for the majority of people, and only those who can traverse the starry sky will be able to move between realms."

It's like burning the only bridge across a raging river!"
"My only concern right now is whether the Stairway to Heaven will return..."
